The FixedQueuePool is created once in the factory __init__ and handed to every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy created by create_with_partitions. Arroyo closes the strategy on each rebalance, and close()/terminate() call queue_pool.shutdown(), which shuts the queues down and stops the workers. The next create_with_partitions reuses the same dead pool (queue_pool is still not None). submit() then hits work_queue.put() on a shut-down queue, which raises queue.ShutDown. The broad except in submit() logs it and marks the offset added and complete, so the offset becomes committable although the message was never processed.

Unbounded queues give no backpressure
The docstring promises natural backpressure, but queue.Queue() is unbounded and submit() never blocks or raises MessageRejected. poll() does not throttle, so a slow processor lets the consumer keep reading and memory grows without limit.

Failed submissions are marked complete and so committed
Any exception during decode, grouping or enqueue is logged and the offset is marked complete. The offset can then be committed, so a transient failure drops the message permanently.

Non-contiguous offsets block commits permanently
The commit scan stops at the first offset missing from all_offsets. If the topic has offset gaps (control records, compaction, filtered messages not submitted), the committed offset never passes the gap. all_offsets then grows without bound and the group re-reads everything after a restart.

Commit called from a background thread; no final commit on close
commit_function, which wraps arroyo's non-thread-safe commit, is called from a separate daemon thread rather than the consumer thread. On close, the loop exits without committing offsets that have completed since the last tick, and workers are shut down afterwards, so progress is lost.
